findings.title: `--check --rehearse` mutates the filesystem despite its read-only contract
findings.description: `deploy/setup-backup.sh:8-9` explicitly promises that `--check` “changes nothing”, but `deploy/setup-backup.sh:133-136` unconditionally runs `mkdir -p "$REHEARSE"` before the step loop, even when `CHECK=1`. That means every `_check(host)` invocation in `test/unit/test_setup_backup.py` creates the rehearsal directory. The tests only assert that `host["root"]`, `host["rehearse"]/clusters`, and `host["rehearse"]/cron.d` do not exist; they never assert that `host["rehearse"]` itself is absent, so the contract violation is not caught. Guard the `mkdir` with `[ "$CHECK" -eq 0 ]`, or defer directory creation to the apply path, and add a test that `--check --rehearse` leaves no new path behind.

findings.title: The cutover’s “report is still written” guarantee only covers two exception types
findings.description: `scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py:269-284` catches only `StepFailed` and `subprocess.CalledProcessError`; `scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py:287-313` has no `try/finally` around report writing. Ordinary failures can therefore bypass the documented recovery record: for example, `scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py:224` calls `(ctx.main.backup_root / "backup-health.log").read_text().splitlines()[-1]`, which raises `FileNotFoundError` or `IndexError` if the log is missing or empty; preflight `CRON_FILE.read_text()` in `main()` can raise `FileNotFoundError`; and `shell()`/`run()` can raise `OSError`. The project’s Python rules allow a documented top-level process-boundary handler, but this one is missing. `test/unit/test_cutover_227.py`’s `test_failed_step_stops_later_steps_and_report_still_written` only builds the report string via `render_report`; it never exercises `main()` writing the file after a failure. Add a top-level handler/finally that records the unexpected exception in the current step, writes the report, and exits non-zero; then test `main()`’s failure path.

findings.title: Production-cron comparison hard-codes a value owned by the cluster table
findings.description: `scripts/cutover_227_helpers.py:84-88` strips `" --replication-host 127.0.0.1"` with a literal, while `deploy/lib/render_cron.sh:105-106` derives the same argument from `deploy/backup-clusters.conf`’s `replication_host` column. `scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py#step_apply` calls `production_changes(...)` without passing `ctx.main.replication_host`, so changing the table’s production row to any other host would make the cutover report “production cron lines changed beyond the new arguments” and stop, even though the render is correct. `test/unit/test_setup_backup.py` also hard-codes the same `127.0.0.1` in `_NEW_MAIN_ARGS`, so the tests would not catch the divergence. This violates the project convention “Never scatter comparison values across code”; pass the expected host from the parsed `BackupCluster` into `strip_new_args`/`production_changes` and use the same source in tests.

findings.title: Generated cutover notes omit required frontmatter status
findings.description: `scripts/cutover_227_helpers.py:129-140` emits `docType`, `slice`, `project`, `dateCreated`, and `dateUpdated`, but no `status`. `project-documents/ai-project-guide/file-naming-conventions.md:18-29` defines `status` as a universal required YAML frontmatter field for all markdown documents, and `AGENTS.md` repeats that all markdown files must include the specified frontmatter. Existing cutover reports follow the fuller shape—e.g. `scripts/cutover_265_trades.py:517-520` emits `status: complete|in_progress`. The `outcome` argument is currently only used in the body at `scripts/cutover_227_helpers.py:144`; add `status: complete` for PASS and `status: in_progress` for FAIL, and assert the full frontmatter schema in `test/unit/test_cutover_227.py`.

findings.title: New provisioning tests assert source text rather than behavior
findings.description: Several TD5 tests in `test/unit/test_provision_tick_lib.py:176-258` extract shell function bodies with `_script_function`/`_script_assignments` and then assert literal strings: `test_only_trading_tick_is_created`, `test_parent_directories_755_data_directory_700`, `test_roles_are_applied_with_replication`, and `test_roles_sql_grants_replication_only_when_asked` at `test/unit/test_provision_tick_lib.py:250-258`. These will pass if the literal appears in a comment or inert branch and fail if behavior-preserving formatting changes, while not proving that `scripts/provision_tick_cluster.sh` actually passes `-v with_replication=1`, that `scripts/provision_tick_roles.sql` grants `REPLICATION` when executed, or that parent modes are applied by `--check`/apply. The testing standards call out “tests that assert implementation rather than behavior” as debt. Keep the rendering test for `hba_content`, but cover the replication grant and directory modes by executing the script against stubs/fixtures or by asserting on its `--check`/apply output.

findings.title: The offsite push result and output are ignored in step 11
findings.description: `scripts/cutover_227_tick_backup.py:207-217` calls `shell(tick_commands()["push"], step)` and immediately proceeds to the three `rclone check` calls without inspecting the returned `subprocess.CompletedProcess`. `scripts/cutover_227_host.py:53-57` captures stdout/stderr but only appends `$ command` to `step.seen`; it does not record the push’s output or exit code. `scripts/sync_wal_offsite.sh` exits non-zero and logs a failure message to stderr when `rclone copy` fails, so a failed push can leave the WAL stamp untouched while the cutover report contains no evidence of that failure. Even if the subsequent checks sometimes catch the discrepancy, the step should not depend on that indirect signal. Record the result with `record()` or equivalent, require `returncode == 0`, and include stdout/stderr in `step.seen`; add a test where the push fails but the checks are stubbed clean.
